blocks.what_we_do: Compare three ways to decide which p-values are small enough to call a result: the usual GWAS threshold, a Bonferroni threshold for this scan and a false-discovery-rate adjustment.
blocks.why:
Running many tests at once is called [multiple testing](docs/glossary.md#multiple-testing). Every test has a small chance of a false positive, so many tests give many chances. The [Bonferroni correction](docs/glossary.md#bonferroni) handles this simply. We choose an error rate alpha, for example 0.05. We divide it by the number of tests. The result is the p-value threshold. This keeps the chance of even one false positive at or below alpha, also when the tests are correlated.

The usual GWAS threshold is 5e-8, which means 0.00000005. It is called [genome-wide significance](docs/glossary.md#genome-wide-significance). It is about 0.05 divided by one million common-variant tests. It is a convention. It is not a guarantee for every ancestry, every study design or every set of tests.

The Benjamini-Hochberg (BH) method controls a different quantity. This quantity is the [false discovery rate](docs/glossary.md#false-discovery-rate), the expected share of false results among the results that we call significant. Decide which tests belong to the family before you look at the results.
blocks.you_need: The valid additive results from the summary statistics file made at step 6.8. Do not replace p-values that failed with other values.
blocks.command:
```{r s7-4}
stats <- guided_summary_stats(cfg)
p <- stats$p_value[valid_p(stats$p_value)]
threshold <- data.frame(rule = c("Conventional GWAS", "Bonferroni for this scan", "BH adjusted p at 0.05"),
  threshold = c(5e-8, 0.05 / length(p), 0.05),
  discoveries = c(sum(p < 5e-8), sum(p < 0.05 / length(p)), sum(p.adjust(p, method = "BH") < 0.05)))
print(threshold)
guided_write(threshold, guided_path(cfg, "7.4", "thresholds.tsv"))
```

blocks.expected_result:
There are 236,815 finite tests, so the Bonferroni threshold for this scan is approximately 2.11e-7. The usual threshold gives eight discoveries. BH answers a different question about errors, so it can return more.

The tested PLINK version is set in `config.R` and recorded in
`software_versions.txt`. Validation: the executable chunks, the comparisons with the expected results and the final plot checks passed on Windows.
blocks.troubleshooting: Stop at the first error. Check the input file that R names and the previous step. Keep the command and the messages from the console. Do not use files from a different version of the dataset. See [troubleshooting](docs/troubleshooting.md).
blocks.quick_check:
Does a false discovery rate of 5% mean that each reported variant has a 5% chance of being false?

<details><summary>Show the answer</summary>

No. The rate describes the whole set of discoveries on average. It is not a probability for each single variant.

</details>
